paper.code_data_availability: No formal data or code availability statement. The paper states that the administrative registers are provided by Statistics Denmark; …

variables_mentioned: start- and end-dates of the job spell
estimated annual hours in the job

registers.role: source register for the labor market spells dataset
source register for the labor market spells dataset

registers.name_in_paper: Employer contributions to the employee pension fund Arbejdsmarkedets Tillaegs Pension (ATP)
registers.role: source data for the labor market spells dataset; covers the universe of workers

registers.name_in_paper: Vacancy dataset (Jobindex A/S online job board)

registers.role: linkage and controls: industry classification of firms (IDA-P, IDA-S, IDA-N)

linkages: The three datasets are merged on the firm ID (CVR number).
Workers are linked to firms through job spells in the labor market spells dataset (CPR-number to CVR-number).

Workers' CPR numbers are used to match the spells data to IDA, creating a mapping from the IDA establishment ID (LBNR) to the CVR number; the mapping matches more than 90% of the observations in the spells data.
83% of the CVR numbers in the vacancy dataset are matched to the labor market spells dataset.

sample.universe: Danish business-sector firms (CVR numbers) with a VAT account, linked to all legal residents of Denmark aged 15-70
sample.unit_of_observation: firm-month in the monthly vacancy-employment panel; firm-quarter in the quarterly vacancy-output panel
selection_rules: Discard 681,633 advertisements (about one-third) that cannot be merged with the other datasets because they do not include the posting firm's CVR number.

Discard firms that belong to the non-business sector (NACE 2.0: Agriculture, forestry and fishing; Public administration and Defence; Education; Human health and social work; Arts, entertainment and recreation; Other service activities; Activities of households as employers; Activities of extraterritorial organizations).
Discard firms that settle VAT at a semi-annual frequency.
Delete observations on the entry- and exit-periods for entering and exiting firms; for firms with multiple entry and exit events use only data until the first exit event.
Discard firms with fewer than seven consecutive monthly observations.
Discard firms never observed to post an online job advertisement over the 78 months 2003M1-2009M6.
sample.n_observations: 1,298,615 firm-months and 432,961 firm-quarters in the constructed panels; 1,175,549 firm-months in the monthly regressions and 288,180 firm-quarters in the quarterly revenue regressions (253,456 and 208,334 in the value-added regressions)
sample.n_individuals: 20,511 firms in the monthly and quarterly panels; 18,155 firms in the quarterly revenue regressions

construction_notes: Firm employment N_jt is measured on the first day of every month; a worker's firm of primary employment in a month is the firm where the worker has the greatest number of hours worked for that month and the next two calendar months.

Hires H_jt: workers not on firm j's payroll on the first day of month t and on the payroll on the first day of month t+1; split into hires from employment (H^EE) and from non-employment (H^NE) by the newly hired employees' status on the first day of month t.

Separations S_jt: workers on the payroll on the first day of month t and not on the first day of month t+1; split into separations to employment (S^EE) and to non-employment (S^EN) by status on the first day of month t+1.
All flow variables are normalised by firm employment averaged over two months, e.g. h_jt = H_jt/((N_jt + N_jt+1)/2).
Monthly vacancy rate v^M_jt = a_jt/((N_jt + N_jt+1)/2); quarterly vacancy rate v^Q_js = (a_jt + a_jt+1 + a_jt+2)/((N_jt + N_jt+3)/2).
Job spells that start and end within the same calendar month are counted neither in firm employment nor in hires and separations.
Nominal variables are deflated using the Danish consumer price index and expressed in 2009 Danish Kroner.
A worker's measured hourly wage rate at a particular job is constant within the calendar year; the firm's average hourly wage w_jt is computed over all workers employed in month t.
Quarterly revenue R_js and value added Y_js are aggregated from the monthly VAT accounts; they are not contaminated by Statistics Denmark's imputation because semi-annual VAT filers are discarded.

Earlier NACE 1.0 and NACE 1.1 industry codes are recoded to NACE 2.0 using empirical correspondence tables from 2003 and 2007; a firm-year is assigned the industry of the establishment with the largest number of employed workers.

claims.statement: In a static regression without firm fixed effects, posting at least one online job advertisement in month t is associated with a 0.021 higher monthly hiring rate in that month.

treatment.label: Vacancy-posting indicator I^M_jt (extensive margin of recruiting effort)

register_source.value: Jobindex A/S online job advertisement data, merged to firms by CVR number (not a Statistics Denmark register)

definition.value: Takes value 1 if firm j posts one or more online job advertisements in month t and 0 otherwise; the regressor enters with a truncated lag distribution over k = 0,...,6 months

timing.value: month t and its six monthly lags

register_source.value: Labor market spells dataset: a matched employer-employee dataset built at Aarhus University from the Statistics Denmark administrative registers Registerbaseret Arbejdsstyrke Statistik (RAS, 1985-2007) and Beskaeftigelse For Loenmodtagere (BFL, 2008-) plus ATP pension contributions

definition.value: h_jt = H_jt/((N_jt + N_jt+1)/2), where H_jt is the number of workers not on firm j's payroll on the first day of month t and on its payroll on the first day of month t+1, and N_jt is firm employment measured on the first day of month t

timing.value: month t (contemporaneous with the lag-0 regressor)

units.value: hiring rate, i.e. hires in the month divided by firm employment averaged over two months; 0.01 = 1 percentage point

magnitude.interpretation: 2.1 percentage points, i.e. by one-third of the no-vacancy baseline (Pi/beta = 0.329)

estimand.target_population: Danish business-sector firms observed monthly over 2003M1-2009M6 that post at least one online job advertisement at some point in the observation period (20,511 firms)
estimand.time_horizon: contemporaneous month only (static specification)

population.selection: Firms never observed to post an online job advertisement over the 78 months 2003M1-2009M6 are discarded; firms in the non-business sector and firms that settle VAT at a semi-annual frequency are discarded; entry- and exit-period observations are deleted and, for firms with several entry/exit events, only data up to the first exit are used; firms with fewer than seven consecutive monthly observations are discarded.

identification.source_of_variation: Cross-firm and within-firm monthly variation in Vacancy-posting indicator I^M_jt over 2003-2009, conditional on industry dummies, month dummies, month dummies interacted with industry dummies; the authors state that the estimated parameters do not warrant a causal interpretation.

key_assumptions.assumption: A firm is interpreted as having a vacant position when it posts an online job advertisement; the authors note that a firm may have a vacant position without posting online, and that one advertisement may refer to several positions, which would raise the estimated effect.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The authors state both caveats explicitly and note that no-vacancy hiring is allowed for in the specification.

key_assumptions.assumption: The estimation sample conditions on firms that are observed to post at least one online job advertisement during the 78 months 2003M1-2009M6; firms never observed posting are discarded.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Appendix A.2 and Table A.1 compare the firms with and without observed online advertisements; the retained firms are about five times larger and account for 72% of employment.

key_assumptions.assumption: The lag distribution is truncated at six lags.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The authors report that longer lags are statistically and quantitatively insignificant and do not affect the estimates of other parameters.

key_assumptions.assumption: Recruiting effort that is imperfectly correlated with vacancy-posting is unmeasured and is partially absorbed by the baseline no-vacancy hiring rate and the firm fixed effects; the authors state that the estimated parameters document correlations and do not warrant a causal interpretation.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Stated in Section 3 and in the firm-heterogeneity discussion; no attempt is made to rule it out.

register_source.value: VAT accounts dataset: Statistics Denmark firm panel of monthly revenues and purchases by CVR number, 2001-2012

definition.value: Growth in log quarterly revenue, Delta r_js, entered through a linear spline with a single knot at the cross-sectional standard deviation of growth and a truncated lag distribution over k = 0,...,6 quarters; this term covers growth up to one cross-sectional standard deviation in absolute value

timing.value: quarter s and its six quarterly lags

register_source.value: Jobindex A/S online job advertisement data, merged to firms by CVR number (not a Statistics Denmark register)

definition.value: Number of advertisements posted by firm j in quarter s divided by average employment of quarters s and s+1: v^Q_js = (a_jt + a_jt+1 + a_jt+2)/((N_jt + N_jt+3)/2)

timing.value: quarter s

units.value: quarterly vacancy rate, i.e. advertisements posted in the quarter divided by firm employment averaged over two quarters; 0.01 = 1 percentage point

estimand.target_population: Danish business-sector firms observed quarterly over 2003Q1-2009Q2 that post at least one online job advertisement at some point in the observation period
estimand.time_horizon: cumulative response over the contemporaneous quarter and six quarterly lags

population.description: Danish business-sector firms observed quarterly over 2003Q1-2009Q2 that post at least one online job advertisement at some point in the observation period
population.selection: Firms never observed to post an online job advertisement over the 78 months 2003M1-2009M6 are discarded; firms in the non-business sector and firms that settle VAT at a semi-annual frequency are discarded; entry- and exit-period observations are deleted and, for firms with several entry/exit events, only data up to the first exit are used; firms with fewer than seven consecutive monthly observations are discarded.

identification.source_of_variation: Within-firm quarterly variation in Small over 2003-2009, conditional on quarter dummies, industry dummies, quarter dummies interacted with industry dummies and firm fixed effects; the authors state that the estimated parameters do not warrant a causal interpretation.

key_assumptions.assumption: A firm is interpreted as having a vacant position when it posts an online job advertisement; the authors note that a firm may have a vacant position without posting online, and that one advertisement may refer to several positions, which would raise the estimated effect.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The authors state both caveats explicitly and note that no-vacancy hiring is allowed for in the specification.

key_assumptions.assumption: The estimation sample conditions on firms that are observed to post at least one online job advertisement during the 78 months 2003M1-2009M6; firms never observed posting are discarded.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Appendix A.2 and Table A.1 compare the firms with and without observed online advertisements; the retained firms are about five times larger and account for 72% of employment.

implies_edges.from: ever posts an online job advertisement 2003M1-2009M6

key_assumptions.assumption: The lag distribution is truncated at six lags.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The authors report that longer lags are statistically and quantitatively insignificant and do not affect the estimates of other parameters.

key_assumptions.assumption: Recruiting effort that is imperfectly correlated with vacancy-posting is unmeasured and is partially absorbed by the baseline no-vacancy hiring rate and the firm fixed effects; the authors state that the estimated parameters document correlations and do not warrant a causal interpretation.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Stated in Section 3 and in the firm-heterogeneity discussion; no attempt is made to rule it out.

implies_edges.to: Small (symmetric) quarterly revenue growth, growth up to one cross-sectional standard deviation in absolute value

threats_discussed: A firm can have a vacant position without posting an online job advertisement (other recruiting channels).
One advertisement may refer to several positions, which would raise the estimated effect of vacancy-posting on hiring.
About one-third of advertisements cannot be merged because they carry no CVR number.
Firms with no observed online advertisements are discarded and are mostly a source of mismeasurement.
robustness_checks: Regressions re-run with the linear-spline knot at 0.5 and 2 standard deviations of revenue growth (results quantitatively very similar, omitted).
unresolved_confounders: Recruiting effort that is imperfectly correlated with vacancy-posting is not measured and is likely partially absorbed by the baseline no-vacancy hiring rate and the firm fixed effects.

given: quarter dummies interacted with industry dummies

ambiguities: Eq. (5) as printed multiplies the lag weights by range indicators only, while Eq. (6) and the reported Omega values multiply the cumulative weights by Delta r, i.e. the specification is a linear spline; the equation is transcribed as printed.
The authors attribute the absence of a relationship to strong non-linearities that the specification captures poorly.

value.as_printed: z_js = beta + sum_{k=0}^{6} pi^+_{S,k} 1(Delta r_{j,s-k} in (0, sigma_{Delta r}]) + sum_{k=0}^{6} pi^+_{L,k} 1(Delta r_{j,s-k} in (sigma_{Delta r}, infinity)) + sum_{k=0}^{6} pi^-_{S,k} 1(Delta r_{j,s-k} in [-sigma_{Delta r}, 0)) + sum_{k=0}^{6} pi^-_{L,k} 1(Delta r_{j,s-k} in (-infinity, -sigma_{Delta r})) + x'_js delta + rho_j + epsilon_js
value.lhs: z_js, either the quarterly vacancy-posting indicator I^Q_js (a linear probability model) or the quarterly vacancy rate v^Q_js
value.parameter_of_interest: Pi^+_S, Pi^+_L, Pi^-_S, Pi^-_L: the cumulative lag-weight sums for small/large positive and negative output-growth shocks
value.normalisation: beta is the no-shock baseline (the predicted vacancy-posting probability or vacancy rate when there is no output-growth shock); the spline knot is the cross-sectional standard deviation of growth, sigma_{Delta r}; no omitted event-time category.

outcomes_examined_not_reported: Regressions with the linear-spline knot at 0.5 and 2 standard deviations: described as quantitatively very similar and omitted.

regressors: Pi_S (dynamic, non-linear, symmetric; small shocks)
target_designation.reasoning: The parameter is defined in the estimating equation of this section and is the quantity the table and the accompanying text report.
